newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht lower, interbank rate rises late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht lower, interbank rate rises late.

text.p: The Thai baht dipped further against the dollar in late Thursday trade the on U.S. unit's strengthening abroad and commercial demand for the dollar, dealers said.

The baht was quoted at 25.830/25.850 to the dollar in the local market against 25.810/25.830 in the early morning. In the offshore market, the baht was traded at around 25.600/25.640 compared with 25.750/25.800 early.
The central bank fixed the mid-rate at 25.75 per dollar versus 25.71 on Wednesday.
"There was commercial buying of the dollar. The interbank market remained quiet as most local banks already squared their positions," said one dealer at a foreign bank.

The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was steady at 15/25 satangs late in the onshore market, unchanged from in the early morning. In the offshore market, the premium was at 40/60 satangs versus 40/70 earlier.
The overnight interbank rate rose to 10.50-12.00 percent late from 10.00 in the morning on tightening liquidity, dealers said.
"Dollar buying in the foreign exchange market had some impact on market liquidity," said one money market dealer.
